question: When does a system listed in Annex III escape the high-risk class?

citations.label: Article 6(3)
citations.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems

citations.label: Article 6(2)
citations.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems

citations.label: Annex III, point 4
citations.title: High-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2)

answer: An Annex III system is high-risk by default [Article 6(2)]. It is not high-risk when it does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision making [Article 6(3)]. That covers a narrow procedural task, improving the result of a completed human activity, detecting decision patterns without replacing the human assessment, or a preparatory task. The exemption never applies when the system profiles natural persons [Article 6(3)]. For example, a tool that filters job applications is listed in [Annex III, point 4] and stays high-risk if it ranks candidates.
